title: Securing the Jackpot: How Western Canada Lottery Corporation Is Modernizing 5,000 Retail Sites with Netskope SASE
summary: Western Canada Lottery Corporation is a non-profit organization that operates lottery products for Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and three northern territories. With 5,000 retail lottery terminal locations across one of the world’s largest and most geographically dispersed retail networks, WCLC set out to consolidate a fragmented multi-ISP infrastructure, cut multi-million dollar circuit costs, modernize employee and vendor access, and govern AI adoption, all on a single unified SASE platform.
body_markdown: For Western Canada Lottery Corporation (WCLC), a non-profit organization serving the lottery needs of Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta, and three northern territories, operational continuity isn’t just a technical goal. It’s a community obligation. Every dollar of efficiency the organization finds flows directly back to the provinces it serves, funding priority programs and services within the region. With 5,000 retail lottery terminal locations dispersed across some of the most geographically vast and remote terrain in Canada, WCLC needed to consolidate a fragmented, multi-ISP retail network, replacing a sprawl of point products with a single Netskope One SASE at every site, while securing employee access and governing AI adoption. The result: reduced cost, reduced complexity, and streamlined operations across 5,000 retail sites.
